title: Staged release entitlements and rollback authorization framework
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Summary: Define and ship a conservative, auditable entitlement and sign-off framework that governs staged model releases (canaries, A/B, shadow) and ties automated rollback gates to both metric thresholds and human approvals. This ticket covers the product requirements, UI flows in Console, necessary API surface, and the governance model used by Dedicated/Private deployments.

Background: As more customers adopt canary and shadow traffic patterns, we need stronger guardrails to meet security and compliance requests. Current rollout controls are lightweight (percentage knobs + basic canary windows) and lack: role-based signoff bindings, timebound approvals, cryptographic approval provenance, and a consistent audit log schema across environments. This causes friction for enterprise customers requesting mandated signoffs and makes post-incident attribution harder.

Goals:
- Provide an entitlement matrix that maps impact level to required approvers and RBAC groups.
- Implement time-limited approval tokens and a reversible approval ledger recorded in the audit log.
- Surface a compact sign-off UI in Console that can be integrated into automation (APIs and webhook hooks).
- Wire rollout gates to observable signals (error rate, latency p95, quality regressions) and require either auto-green metrics or explicit signoff to progress past each stage.
- Ensure auto-rollback triggers are recorded with the same provenance (who/what caused the rollback), and allow manual override with an escalation clause.

Proposed design (high level):
- Entitlement matrix: impact tiers (none, low, medium, high) defined by expected request volume + customer SLO sensitivity. Each tier maps to a set of required groups: deployer, security approvers, data-ops reviewer, and legal for high-impact. RBAC ties to SSO groups (SCIM) for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Sign-off tokens: ephemeral cryptographically-signed tokens issued when an approver clicks "Approve" in Console or calls the approvals API. Tokens expire after configured TTL (default 72h) and are attached to rollout records.
- Approval ledger & audit log: add standardized events (approval_request_created, approval_granted, approval_revoked, auto_rollback_triggered, manual_rollback_initiated) with fields: timestamp, principal, token_id, reason, linked_metrics_snapshot, related_pr_url. Stored in the central audit store (and forwarded to customer-managed sinks for Private).
- Gating rules: declarative gate objects for each stage (canary, A/B ramp, full): conditions include metric expressions (e.g., service.error_rate > 0.02 for 5m), regression delta thresholds (embedding-quality-drop > 1.5%), and a boolean require_signoff. If require_signoff is true, progression stops until tokens from all required approvers exist.
- Auto-rollback: automated policy evaluates gates continuously during ramp. If a gate fails, system records auto_rollback_triggered and reverses traffic to previous model; notifications are emitted (email/Slack/webhook). Manual override is allowed only if a higher-tier approver provides a signed override token with an explanation and expiry.

APIs & Console changes:
- New REST endpoints: POST /rollouts/:id/approval-requests, POST /rollouts/:id/approve, GET /rollouts/:id/audit-events.
- Console: compact signoff modal shows required approvers, time-limited token TTL, linked metrics and snapshot button, and a cryptographic token preview for copy-to-automation.

Privacy & compliance:
- Audit records respect data retention policies and are redactable per legal requests. For Private deployments, customers can opt to keep approval vaults and token signing keys on customer-managed KMS.

Open questions / trade-offs:
1) Token model vs. simple boolean approvals: tokens allow third-party automation and non-repudiation but add KMS/key rotation complexity.
2) How prescriptive should the entitlement matrix be vs. flexible templates per org? We'll ship a sensible default plus org templates.
3) Whether to require cryptographic signing for Hosted customers at launch or roll that out later as an enterprise feature.

Risks:
- Increased latency for rollouts if approval workflows are misconfigured; we will add sane defaults and an emergency fast-path for SRE.
- Key management complexity for Private; mitigation: partner with infra/security to provide clear onboarding docs and KMS integration playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Entitlement matrix UI in Console with editable templates and default mapping for impact tiers
Approval API endpoints implemented with token issuance and TTL enforcement
Approval events written to audit log with standardized event types and fields
Gating rules support metric expressions and require_signoff flag; gates block progress until satisfied
Auto-rollback policy executes on gate failure and records provenance; notifications sent to configured channels
Dedicated/Private option to use customer-managed KMS for token signing documented
End-to-end e2e test that simulates a canary ramp with a failing metric and verifies auto-rollback and audit entries
